instruction: Run `C:\Users\user\Desktop\sallen_key.cir` in native PSpice. Keep the native simulator artifacts as `C:\Users\user\Desktop\sallen_key.out`, `C:\Users\user\Desktop\sallen_key_measure.txt`, and `C:\Users\user\Desktop\sallen_key.dat`. Then read the nine corner measurement blocks from `C:\Users\user\Desktop\sallen_key_measure.txt` and write `C:\Users\user\Desktop\wc.json` with `BW_nominal`, `BW_min`, `BW_max`, `corner_min`, and `corner_max`, where each `BW_*` value is the highest sample frequency at which that corner's peak remains within 3 dB. `corner_min` and `corner_max` must each be an object with numeric `RSCALE` and `CSCALE` fields. They identify the corner producing `BW_min` or `BW_max`; if multiple corners tie, use the first tied corner in the measurement order. [Software] Use the native PSpice command-line simulator `C:\Cadence\SPB_24.1\tools\bin\psp_cmd.exe`. In this image, use `C:\Cadence\SPB_24.1\tools\bin\Capture.exe` for OrCAD schematics and `C:\Cadence\SPB_24.1\tools\bin\allegro.exe` for board work.
